automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Visible publication or update timestamp must fall within the preceding 48 hours; date-only, ambiguous, future-dated, and boundary-only candidates are excluded.

local_context_checked.duplicate_check: Searched local raw, raw/processed, and docs/wiki for selected CVE identifiers. CVE-2026-115726/Aider was already captured and synthesized; it is excluded.

source_method.primary_source: NVD CVE API v2.0 public vulnerability database query for 2026-10-22 through 2026-10-24, followed by per-record inspection.
source_method.limitations: NVD is concrete public disclosure evidence but several records need maintainer-advisory or release-note confirmation during ingest.

qualifying_findings.summary: GitLab EE group Owners could re-enable Duo AI-backed data egress after an instance administrator locked the group's Duo availability, because the lock was not enforced with sufficient granularity.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: GitLab EE 19.2 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An administrative control intended to prevent third-party AI data transfer could be overridden by a delegated group role.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: GitLab and Duo product context belongs in ai-wiki; retain the delegated AI-egress lock enforcement boundary in this security wiki.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: During ingest, confirm GitLab's primary advisory and verify whether the lock must be audited on existing descendant projects.

qualifying_findings.summary: agentjido req_llm's WebSocket streaming client disabled certificate verification and discarded caller TLS options, enabling an on-path attacker to read or alter OpenAI WebSocket sessions and bearer tokens.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: req_llm 1.9.0 before 1.29.0; OpenAI Responses, Realtime, and Codex WebSocket paths are named as affected.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI API credentials and streamed model interactions cross a TLS trust boundary that the affected client made non-verifying.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Framework and OpenAI product background belongs in ai-wiki; keep the certificate-validation and token-channel failure locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the 1.29.0 release remediation and identify deployments using the WebSocket rather than HTTP streaming path.

qualifying_findings.summary: AgenticSeek's llm_server bound Flask debug mode to all interfaces; a reachable attacker able to obtain the derivable debugger PIN could execute Python and OS commands as the service.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An LLM-serving control plane exposed a development debugger as an unauthenticated remote-code-execution surface.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AgenticSeek product context belongs in ai-wiki; retain its public model-server and debugger exposure boundary here.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Reconcile the fixing commit with a maintained release and assess whether affected listeners were internet-reachable.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related approval-control cluster
qualifying_findings.summary: PraisonAI dangerous-tool approvals could be accepted by unrelated Discord-channel text, skipped by recipe streaming, or self-approved through XSS in the HTTP approval dashboard.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI 4.5.2 or 4.5.87 before 4.6.59, depending on component; all three records name 4.6.59 as patched.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Human-in-the-loop authorization for autonomous actions fails if approvals are not request-bound, enforced consistently, and rendered safely.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI background belongs in ai-wiki; keep this security-specific approval and action-gate cluster locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Split into request-binding, policy-parity, and approval-UI leaves during ingest; confirm 4.6.59 upgrade coverage.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related filesystem-boundary cluster
qualifying_findings.summary: PraisonAI Dynamic Context and artifact helper tools accepted caller-controlled identifiers or paths, allowing traversal and reads outside configured history or artifact roots, including readable credentials and local files.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt- or tool-controlled arguments must not become host filesystem authority in agent context and artifact tools.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI context-tool catalog belongs in ai-wiki; retain the host-file authorization boundary in this wiki.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Assess logs, context stores, and artifact helpers separately; verify normalized-path and containment checks in the patch.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related channel and listener authentication cluster
qualifying_findings.summary: PraisonAI bypassed Slack allowlists on app mentions, exposed a deprecated Recipe HTTP server without authentication, and accepted forged Linear webhook events when its secret was absent.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI 3.11.0 or 4.5.112 or 4.6.56 before 4.6.59; patched in 4.6.59.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted chat events or public service listeners can invoke agents with bot credentials and delegated actions.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: PraisonAI and channel integrations are upstream-owned product context; retain the invocation-authorization and public-listener implications locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Audit all deployed bot event routes, secrets, allowlist parity, and public recipe listeners before accepting the patched version.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related OpenAPI-fetch control cluster
qualifying_findings.summary: mcp-from-openapi forwarded Authorization and Cookie headers across cross-origin redirects and allowed trailing-dot hostnames to bypass its SSRF blocked-host denylist when fetching attacker-controlled specs or redirects.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-from-openapi 2.5.0 before 2.9.0 for credential exposure; Agentfront mcp-from-openapi 2.2.0 before 2.9.0 for SSRF.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool-generation from untrusted API specifications can transfer credentials or access operator-blocked network destinations.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP and product catalog coverage belongs in ai-wiki; this wiki owns redirect credential forwarding and SSRF denylist normalization.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm 2.9.0 fixes and test redirect credential stripping plus canonical hostname validation.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related MCP exposure and code-execution findings
qualifying_findings.summary: NetBox MCP HTTP transport lacked authentication before 1.2.1, while SageMath, Git, and Docker MCP server packages exposed remote command-execution paths in their named functions.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NetBox MCP Server before 1.2.1; @justice8096/sagemath-mcp-server, @rog0x/mcp-git-tools, and @rog0x/mcp-docker-tools version 1.0.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Reachable MCP services may grant tool authority without authentication or safely bounded command construction.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP-server catalog entries belong in ai-wiki; keep listener authentication and remote-execution boundaries locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: During ingest, obtain maintainer advisories or patches for the three 1.0.1 packages and split the NetBox authentication issue from execution issues.

qualifying_findings.summary: Uni-CLI's legacy loopback JSON-RPC-over-HTTP MCP transport accepted browser CORS-simple POSTs without Origin validation, allowing a malicious page to drive local tools/call requests; Streamable HTTP did enforce that boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A browser page can cross into a locally running agent tool server unless every transport applies the same browser-to-localhost authorization rule.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Uni-CLI product context belongs in ai-wiki; retain transport-parity and browser-to-localhost authority analysis here.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Inventory legacy JSON-RPC MCP listeners and upgrade or disable them; verify Origin enforcement independently.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database record with AWS service-side remediation note
qualifying_findings.summary: An incomplete disallowed-input list in AWS MCP Server's run_script Python validator could permit crafted code execution in the authenticated user's isolated session; AWS states it fixed the service-side issue and requires no customer action.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AWS MCP Server run_script tool; no customer version or deployment action stated.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Code-validation deny lists are not a durable execution boundary even when a tool session is isolated.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AWS and MCP service context belongs in ai-wiki; retain the code-validator assurance and provider-remediation boundary locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Locate AWS's primary bulletin and clarify residual tenant, session, and audit implications before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.summary: UbiquitousLearning mllm load_model accepted a manipulated shard_file path, producing local path traversal through version 2.0.2; the record reports public exploit availability and no project response.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mllm up to 2.0.2; pymllm/mobile/convertor/__init__.py load_model shard_file.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model artifact and shard metadata must be treated as untrusted filesystem input in model-loading pipelines.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: mllm product context belongs in ai-wiki; retain model-artifact path containment as the local supply-chain lens.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Obtain the referenced issue or maintainer response and determine whether a patched release exists before advising upgrades.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records; related LangGraph state and deployment credential findings
qualifying_findings.summary: LangGraph checkpoint savers could resolve unvalidated dotted namespaces into another tenant's stored state, while LangGraph CLI --verbose could print a temporary container-registry push token to logs or terminal recordings.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres before 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite before 3.1.2; LangGraph CLI 0.4.15 through 0.4.32, fixed in 0.4.32.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent state isolation and deployment-token handling are separate but critical data and supply-chain boundaries.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: LangGraph background belongs in ai-wiki and general deployment practice in ai-dev-wiki; retain cross-tenant state and credential-log exposure here.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Split persistence isolation and CLI token logging into separate leaves during ingest; verify all patched versions and rotate potentially logged tokens.

qualifying_findings.summary: MLflow GenAI scorer endpoints accepted serialized third-party scorer data whose selected class and constructor arguments were insufficiently constrained; with optional TruLens/LiteLLM packages, an unauthenticated request could cause outbound requests to attacker-chosen or internal hosts with attacker-controlled headers and body.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MLflow 3.12.0rc0 through 3.17.0; fixed in 3.17.0. Named endpoint includes unauthenticated POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Evaluation tooling can become an unauthenticated deserialization-to-network-egress boundary rather than a passive assurance component.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MLflow product context belongs in ai-wiki and general evaluation practice in ai-dev-wiki; retain scorer deserialization and egress control locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm MLflow's primary advisory, upgrade to 3.17.0, and restrict scorer endpoints plus outbound network access.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD public vulnerability database records with vendor-confirmed internal-ticket references
qualifying_findings.summary: Unitree Go2 chat_go exposed remote OS command injection through gpt_thread.py set_volume and used improper certificate validation in its WebSocket client.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Go2 chat_go through 1.1.11.4 for command injection, fixed in 1.1.11.5; TLS-validation issue affects up to 1.1.13, 1.1.14.1, or 1.1.15.1 according to branch.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An embodied AI assistant's command and TLS channels bridge remote inputs into robot-control software.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Unitree product and robotics context belongs in ai-wiki; retain chat command execution and transport-authentication security implications locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm vendor release notes and exact fixed versions for every Go2 firmware branch before durable synthesis.

exclusions.reason: Already captured in the October 23 collector and synthesized locally; do not duplicate.

exclusions.candidate: CVE-2026-111958 (Royal MCP WordPress preview-token scope bypass)
exclusions.reason: Already represented by a local security leaf and not a new delta for this run.
Subscription entitlement bypass has no concrete AI security, privacy, control, or assurance delta in the record.

exclusions.candidate: Generic vulnerabilities returned because descriptions contain the word agent, model, AI, or LLM in non-AI contexts
exclusions.reason: Keyword presence alone is not an AI-system security boundary.

exclusions.candidate: Ordinary product announcements and non-security feature news
exclusions.reason: No concrete threat, vulnerability, patch, control, assurance, regulatory, or incident change.

exclusions.candidate: Date-only, ambiguous-date, future-dated, and boundary-only source pages
exclusions.reason: The collection rule requires a visible, unambiguous in-window timestamp.

confidence_notes: NVD records supply concrete public disclosure, affected-version, and remediation facts, but NVD-first findings should be reconciled with maintainer advisories before producing durable guidance.
The Unitree records fall inside the window by publication time but are only about ten minutes before this run; retain the exact timestamps.
Grouped findings share a product and security boundary for raw collection only; ingest should split independently maintained security issues into separate leaves where warranted.
follow_up_actions: Ingest each retained finding with primary maintainer advisory or release-note checks, especially medium-confidence records.
Prioritize deployed public MCP listeners, approval channels, model-loading paths, evaluation endpoints, and LangGraph persistence or CI log exposure.
Do not edit docs/wiki or move this artifact to raw/processed until a separate ingest workflow completes verification.
